page: Google Cloud Platform m4n-ultramem-224 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the m4n server family. It features 224 dedicated vCPUs and 5952.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 26.57 GB per vCPU. This configuration is designed specifically for workloads requiring massive memory footprints.

The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes. It also includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring external networking configurations for public access.

Given the massive memory allocation and high vCPU count, this server represents a high-cost tier optimized for resource density rather than budget efficiency. The lack of local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators means workloads must rely entirely on CPU-bound processing and network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy operations.

This server is designed for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, massive data analytics, and other memory-intensive enterprise workloads that require substantial RAM without the need for hardware acceleration.
